structured.reason: The description contains conditional caveats and wear-related reassurance that touch on the complaints in the reviews. (1) "If you have oily or combination lids, apply eyeshadow primer first to help your liner last longer." This is a conditional caveat: the product performs well only with special preparation for certain skin types. (2) "Shoppers often mention how smoothly the liner glides and how well it holds up through the day." This addresses long-wear durability, the same issue as the review complaint "you've got to reapply it all day long," and frames it defensively. (3) "The formula stays put through a rainy commute or an unplanned pool day, which lets you plan your day without worrying about touch-ups." The phrase "without worrying about touch-ups" implicitly reassures against the reapplication complaint. Under the strict standard, these are caveated or minimizing statements about performance, so the description fails.
